newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end up on foreign ownership increase.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end up on foreign ownership increase.

text.p: Stocks ended higher on Saturday as investors bought blue chips ahead of Friday's expansion on the foreign shareholding limit, brokers said.
They said shares are likely to rise further early next week with a support seen at 700.
The composite stock index stood at 699.76 at the close, up 7.28 points from Friday. Advancing issues swamped decliners by 435 to 336.
The ceiling on foreign shareholding will be raised to 23 percent from the current 20 percent.

"The rise in blue chips, especially Samsung Electronics and POSCO, pushed the index up," said Kim Joo-hyeong at KDB Securities. "Institutions bought them ahead of next week's expansion on foreign shareholdings."
Samsung Electronics Co Ltd ended at 61,000 won, up 2,500 won and Pohang Iron and Steel Co ended at 54,000 won, up 500 won.
Traders said they expected the index to fall after Friday as institutions would sell heavily to take profits.
Liquidty was seen tight as the central Bank of Korea siphoned off 1.88 trillion won this week through three repurchase deals, but brokers said it did not affect the market on Saturday.
"With market factors the index should be at about 650 but next week's increase in the foreign limit is keeping the market around 700," said Choi Young-ho at Samsung Securities.
The benchmark three-year corporate bond yields closed at 12.50 percent on Saturday down 0.02 percentage points from Friday's closing.
Volume totalled 32 million shares in half trading on Saturday, compared with 41.6 million on Friday.
